title: Dedicated pool autoscale failures: root cause analysis and RFC for policy hardening
creator: Jorge Martinez
description: Summary: On 2026-02-28 we observed repeated throughput regressions and request errors for multiple Dedicated customers using GPU pools. The symptom was periodic 5-10 minute windows of elevated p99 latency and increased 429/503 errors while overall cluster utilization oscillated. Manual scaling restored capacity but the autoscaler repeatedly overcorrected and bounced capacity causing sustained degradation. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and an RFC/proposed plan to harden autoscaling + fleet controls and update runbooks.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-28T03:12Z: First anomaly alert from SLO monitors: p99 latency for dedicated-pool-eu-west spikes by 120%
2026-02-28T03:17Z: Autoscaler trigger: scale-up +4 GPUs (based on short-window utilization threshold)
2026-02-28T03:20Z: Service instability: new nodes experience elevated cold-start token latencies (kernel selection path changed two days prior)
2026-02-28T03:23Z: Autoscaler observes drop in per-node throughput due to cache warmup and scales down, removing nodes that were mid-warmup
2026-02-28T03:25Z: Client-facing errors increase (429 throttles + occasional 503s). On-call paged.
2026-02-28T03:33Z: Incident commander authorizes manual reservation of +6 GPUs and enables short-term traffic diversion to fallback model-variant
2026-02-28T04:10Z: Latency stabilizes to normal after manual mitigation. Autoscaler still oscillating; temporary autoscaler disable applied for affected pools.
2026-02-28T06:00Z: Full mitigation: autoscaler patched with temporary longer evaluation window and disabled downscale for 15 minutes; observe recovery and post-incident analysis kickoff.
actions_taken: Applied manual capacity reservation to affected pools to absorb immediate load
Enabled fallback model-variant routing for highest-latency routes to reduce per-request cost and cold-starts
Temporarily disabled autoscaler downscales for 15 minutes to prevent immediate evictions during warmup
Raised SLO alert thresholds and created an ad-hoc dashboard showing per-node KV cache hit rates, kernel variant distribution, and cold-start counts
Opened a follow-up to revert the risky kernel selection commit to a canary channel until perf regression is fully measured
root_cause: This incident was caused by a combination of three factors that together produced autoscaler thrash: (1) a recent runtime kernel selection change increased tail latency for cold-started lanes, extending warmup periods for many model variants; (2) the autoscaler decision logic used an instantaneous 30s utilization metric with no hysteresis and aggressively downscaled when utilization dipped during warmups; (3) an admission controller race allowed new requests to be scheduled onto nodes that were still initializing, further amplifying latency and causing utilization feedback loops. Individually these were tolerable; together they created a positive feedback loop of scale-up/scale-down leading to capacity shortfalls and customer-facing errors.
impact_summary: High impact for 3 large Dedicated customers in eu-west and us-central for ~1 hour of degraded performance with error spikes. Estimated 12k USD of lost inference revenue during the incident window and several production alerts in customer monitoring. No data loss or security incidents.
postmortem_summary: Immediate mitigations resolved customer impact. Root cause identified as algorithm + runtime interaction. We propose an RFC to harden autoscaling policies, add explicit warmup-aware signals, and extend runbooks to include coordinated scaling/rollback playbooks. This ticket consolidates concrete action items and owners.
proposed_changes_rfc: High-level proposals: 1) Autoscaler algorithm change to use a weighted moving average of utilization with configurable hysteresis windows and minimum stabilization (avoid downscale < 10m). 2) Introduce an explicit 'warmup' metric (KV-cache-hit-rate + kernel-variant-stability) to suppress downscales until per-node warmup_success >= 80%. 3) Add a safety_capacity headroom param (default +10% GPUs) per pool that prevents full capacity drain when eviction risk is high. 4) Build an autoscaler canary (small fleet) and synthetic workload harness to validate policy changes before global rollout. 5) Add rollback hooks and 'autoscale freeze' API for incident responders.
acceptance_criteria: New autoscaler logic implementation merges and is enabled behind a feature flag
Synthetic harness reproduces previous oscillation locally and demonstrates stability under new policy
Runbook updated with explicit steps to freeze autoscaling, reserve capacity, and switch to fallback model-variants
Dashboards and alerts added: warmup metric, downscale suppression events, safety_capacity headroom utilization
Two customer-facing Dedicated pools run the autoscaler canary for one week with no regressions
action_items: ENG-17250: Implement weighted moving average + hysteresis in autoscaler decision path (owner: Aisha Patel)
ENG-17251: Add warmup-aware signal collection (kv_cache_hit_rate, kernel_variant_stability) and expose as metric (owner: Priya Nanduri)
ENG-17252: Create 'safety_capacity' pool parameter, default +10% headroom; surface in Dedicated console (owner: Ben Chu)
ENG-17253: Build autoscaler canary and synthetic workload harness in CI; include perf regression tests (owner: Infrastructure Team)
ENG-17254: Update incident runbook with new autoscale-freeze and manual-reservation procedures; train on-call rotation (owner: SRE)
ENG-17255: Revert or gate the runtime kernel selection change to canary until warmup profile validated (owner: Runtime Team)
ENG-17256: Add automated alert that fires when autoscaler performs >3 downscale events within 10 minutes (owner: Observability)
ENG-17257: Customer outreach: send incident summary and mitigation steps to impacted customers (owner: Customer Success)
ENG-17258: Postmortem review in next All-Hands and include a brief tech note in release highlights (owner: Engineering Leadership)
review_notes: Design + Runtime + SRE reviewed root cause and agree on moving-average + warmup-signal approach. PM requested a customer communication plan before enabling new autoscaler for GA. Security reviewed and confirmed no secrets exposure. Cost team flagged headroom default may increase committed spend; will reconcile in release gating.
lessons_learned: Autoscaling should never rely solely on short-window instantaneous utilization for downscale decisions
Runtime changes that affect tail latency must be validated against warmup-sensitive workloads in a canary fleet
Operational knobs (freeze autoscale, reserve capacity) are critical for rapid mitigation and should be exposed in the Console
Comms to impacted customers must be templated to speed post-incident outreach
next_steps: Owners assigned to action items above. RFC (ENG-17203-RFC) to be reviewed by 2026-03-18. Plan for canary run starting 2026-04-01 against two low-risk Dedicated pools. Track progress in weekly DedicCapacity Sync.
